message: Non-wrapper runtime binaries must still resolve via command -v and pass shell smoke checks. The unquoted heredoc preserves the backslashes before double quotes in command -v \\"${binary}\\", generating a probe that looks up a binary name containing literal quote characters (e.g. "jq") rather than jq.

Normal runtime binaries must continue to pass shell-based existence and smoke verification. The unquoted heredoc preserves the backslashes before double quotes in command -v, so the generated probe searches for a binary literally named "jq" (including quote characters), not jq. The first manifest entry consequently fails missing_binary:jq even on a healthy image.

Guard against ReDoS via user-controlled regex in custom rules engine. Pattern length and flags checks still accept catastrophic-backtracking patterns such as ^(a+)+$, which run synchronously against allowed short code strings and block the MCP process.

Enforce a maximum file size of 500000 bytes before reading path inputs for execute_custom_rules. The new size guard trusts stat.size without restricting paths to regular files or bounding the actual read, so a special file such as /dev/zero passes with size 0 and is read without limit.

Guard against ReDoS via user-controlled regex in custom rules engine Length limits and flag normalization still admit catastrophic-backtracking patterns such as ^(a+)+$, and execute them synchronously without a timeout.

Allowlisted regex flags must not permit nonterminating custom-rule execution The permitted gu combination still causes the zero-length-match loop to run forever on astral Unicode characters because lastIndex++ advances a UTF-16 unit rather than a Unicode code point.

Fullscreen layout must preserve a usable video player while reserving space for transcript. The max-height limits only the outer wrapper and clips the unchanged aspect-video player instead of resizing it.
VTT parser should accept valid WebVTT timing lines. Timing parsing requires literal single-space delimiters and fails on permitted tabs or extra spaces after the arrow.
VTT cue payload should normalize to visible plain caption text. HTML DOMParser does not remove WebVTT inline timestamp tags; they survive as literal caption text.
Fullscreen lesson layout must keep video and playback controls usable while reserving transcript space. The 45vh cap clips the unchanged full-width aspect-video player instead of resizing it.

Parse legal WebVTT cue timing separators. Timing parsing requires literal spaces and trims the end timestamp only after splitting whitespace, dropping valid cues with tabs or multiple spaces after the arrow.
VTT parsing should produce visible caption text without VTT markup. HTML DOMParser does not strip WebVTT inline timestamp tags.

The new Permissions section must list the permissions required to run the external connection doctor checks. Both authentication tabs list only ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, but doctor searches externalItem entities and retrieves an external item; these operations require external-item permissions, not just external-connection permissions.

The new Permissions section must document sufficient permissions to run external connection doctor, including its content check. Both permission tabs list only ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, but checkContentIngested queries externalItem search and reads an external item; connection management permission does not authorize those item operations. Users granting only the documented permission receive authorization failures reported as failed content checks.

init installs or updates Taskless skills, and info reports installation currency with init as the upgrade remedy. A previous fallback installation is left stale forever once any supported tool becomes detectable: init installs only detected tools and never updates or removes the existing .agents skills, while checkStaleness continues including that fallback.

init installs or updates Taskless skills, including skills previously installed at the universal fallback location After a fallback install, adding a detected tool prevents subsequent init runs from updating the existing .agents skills, although checkStaleness continues to report that installation.

GitHub tree URLs must identify the branch whose manifest and files are fetched. The URL parser discards the explicit branch, and resolveIdentifier unconditionally selects the repository default branch instead.

Remote manifest data must not redirect downloads outside the staging root. skillset.name is used unvalidated in join(tmpdir(), 'spm', skillset.name), allowing .. components to relocate the staging directory; safePath then treats that attacker-selected directory as trusted.

safePath must reject all paths outside the skillset's staging directory. startsWith(baseDir) is a textual prefix check rather than a directory-boundary check and accepts sibling directories sharing the skillset name prefix.

Cross-repository skill sources must fetch a valid ref for their own repository. downloadEntries passes the parent skillset's location.ref to every FileEntry, including entries pointing at a different repository.

GitHub tree URLs select the requested branch for the manifest and files. parseGitHubUrl discards the branch, and resolveIdentifier always uses the repository default branch, so a tree/develop URL installs main instead or fails if the manifest exists only on develop.

Cross-repository skill sources must download from a valid ref in the source repository. downloadEntries assigns location.ref from the manifest repository to every source, including @owner/other-repo/path entries. A manifest repository defaulting to master and a skill repository defaulting to main results in downloads from other-repo/master rather than its default branch.

Remote manifests must not select a write destination outside the staging root. skillset.name is validated only as a string and is passed directly to join(tmpdir(), 'spm', skillset.name). Traversal components in a remote manifest name move tmpDir outside the staging root, after which safePath checks relative to that attacker-chosen directory and writeFile overwrites files there.

safePath must enforce directory containment, not merely a lexical prefix. resolved.startsWith(baseDir) accepts sibling directories whose names begin with the skillset name. For baseDir /tmp/spm/fsd, a result path a/../../fsd-other/foo resolves to /tmp/spm/fsd-other/foo and passes. The resolver accepts such setup/file paths and they can be successfully fetched from a repository branch fsd-other containing foo because fetch normalizes URL dot segments.

Sync helpers must create a persistent reference on first synchronization. syncDocumentReference/syncCollectionReference pass no guid, and upsert's create path never generates one despite the entity using a non-generated primary column.

External identity lookup must match provider/externalId/account/container exactly. Passing literal null for omitted account/container in TypeORM findOne skips these predicates rather than requiring SQL NULL, allowing an unscoped sync to match a scoped reference.

External-reference upserts are keyed by provider, externalId, account and container. findByExternalIdentity passes raw null account/container to TypeORM instead of IsNull(), so omitted scopes are ignored by TypeORM's default null handling and can match another account/container's reference; upsert then overwrites that mapping.

The external reference workflow is an upsert keyed by the four-part external identity. upsertExternalRef performs a separate lookup and insert without a transaction/lock or identity unique constraint. Concurrent syncs for the same new identity can both insert rows.

Bundled doctor and update scripts must validate the repository's actual ao launcher for source-checkout installs. Both newly bundled scripts retain packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js although the wrapper lives at packages/ao/bin/ao.js. Doctor therefore fails a healthy checkout and default update fails its smoke tests.

Bundled source-checkout scripts must validate and smoke-test the actual AO launcher. The newly bundled doctor and update scripts retain the obsolete packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js launcher path; the actual launcher is packages/ao/bin/ao.js.

Public issue requires pagination to be sent as a JSON request body on GET for all three recipients endpoints. All three new methods instead put page/per_page in the URL query and omit the JSON body, so the documented body-based API does not receive pagination in its expected location.

Public issue requires recipients pagination to be serialized as a JSON request body on GET requests. All three recipients methods instead append page and per_page to the URL and omit the request body, failing the stated API pagination contract.
Renamed backend must remain launchable via production container Docker CMD still launches src/webapp/server.js, which is removed by TypeScript migration.
IDE MCP stdio launch must continue functioning VS Code MCP config still invokes node src/webapp/mcp-server.js after rename to .ts.
PowerShell launcher should start renamed webapp start.ps1 still invokes node on server.js instead of TypeScript runtime/server.ts.
Production container must launch the converted backend. Docker CMD still launches removed server.js after rename to server.ts.
IDE MCP configuration must launch the converted MCP service. VS Code MCP config still uses node src/webapp/mcp-server.js, which was renamed to TypeScript.
PowerShell webapp launcher must launch converted backend. start.ps1 still executes node against removed server.js.

Raw SVG imports must deliver SVG markup to createUiIcon. The general asset/resource rule also matches SVG imports with ?raw and overrides the earlier javascript/auto rule; raw-loader output is emitted as an asset and the import is a URL rather than markup. createUiIcon encodes that URL as SVG, producing broken header/navigation icons.

Raw SVG imports must deliver SVG text to createUiIcon Overlapping webpack rules process ?raw SVG imports as asset/resource, so createUiIcon encodes an asset URL rather than SVG markup and header/menu icons fail to render.

New English feature documentation must accurately describe attachment handling in the supplied script. README calls attachment export optional, but every attachment is unconditionally copied to the destination folder, with no opt-out in setup or script.

Cached statistics should remain a consistent snapshot until explicitly refreshed. Reusing Statistics also reuses its un-copied Note references, while MonthChart recalculates day counts from those references on each dialog construction/filter change. Editing a retained note changes the monthly heatmap but leaves cached totals, yearly/weekly maps and phrases unchanged.

Only the currently active statistics load may clear or publish the shared cache/loading state. progressCanceled unconditionally clears shared statistics and loading even for an obsolete loader. A canceled loader can emit cancellation again: chunkComplete emits it immediately while run still waits for futures, and a subsequent worker exception emits it again in run's catch. If the user has started a replacement load in between, the old callback clears its state.

Cached statistics should consistently represent the last gathering until manually refreshed. Reusing Statistics retains mutable Note references while the Months chart recomputes counts from their text. Editing a retained note between dialog visits changes Months values without refreshing the cached overview, year/week totals or phrases.
